name: Himeji-jo
description: Perched on a hill in the city of Himeji, in Hyōgo Prefecture, this dazzling white castle is often called the White Egret Castle because it seems to be taking flight. Its 83 wooden buildings, rebuilt in the early 1600s, are linked by winding approaches designed to confuse attackers. It is Japan's most visited castle, and it came through wartime bombing and the 1995 earthquake intact.
